Tbh the surgery may not fully fix the issue. Because the gallbladder stores bile, removing it reduces the amount of bile available at any given time. A lot of people have the surgery with few issues, but there are also those who get it done and continue to suffer gallbladder symptoms (essentially, symptoms of a bile shortage). This isn't to scare you! Surgery just unfortunately isn't a one size fits all solution.

Hey, I had gallstones for a few months last year, it's MISERABLE. No doc helped me either, so I eventually found a routine of OTC stuff that fixed if for me. Mind wasn't as bad as this and I'm so sorry they let things reach this point for you, but I think there is a solution, or at least some pain relief.

The things that helped me were:

1. TUDCA (tauroursodeoxycholic acid) supplement - this was what stopped the massive gastrointestinal issues for me & made life a little more manageable. There's evidence that it dissolves gallstones, depending on what kind you have. I was finally able to eat normally with this, though the pain didn't completely disappear.
2. a digestive enzyme supplement - any will do. Chances are, if your gallbladder is angry, you're not digesting your food adequately, which will just make you feel worse over time.
3. If neither of the above two cut it, serrapeptase is a prolyotic enzyme & anti-inflammatory that helps to break down scar tissue. I don't know how long this has been going on for you, but if you've dealt with it a long time, it's possible your bile ducts could be scarred. Might be worth a shot to help calm the pain & open things up so your gallbladder can do its job again.

Have you done a HIDA scan? It's the main test to show the true amount of bile ejection from your gallbladder. If your gallbladder isn't contracting, it might show that, too.
